## El Ocaso near Salento: from coffee cherry to cup

Visiting **El Ocaso** near [Salento](/colombia/place/salento/) lets you see how coffee is grown and turned into a drink. The farm lies at approximately **1,500 m** in the Central Andes, among coffee plantations, green slopes and humid mountain forest. The excursion takes place in the afternoon.

Unlike a tasting in an ordinary café, this experience follows the whole production cycle: cherries growing on bushes, hand-picking, processing, drying, roasting and brewing.

## Plantations and hand-picking

At [El Ocaso farm](/colombia/place/el-ocaso-coffee-farm/), a local specialist explains how coffee is cultivated. The ripening of cherries depends on elevation, temperature, rainfall and plant care. During the excursion you learn about hand-picking and why selecting fruit at the right stage of ripeness is important for high-quality raw materials.

The coffee cherry is a fruit with seeds inside. Once processed and dried, those seeds are called coffee beans. Green, ripe and overripe cherries differ, so selective picking affects the subsequent stages.

The tour demonstrates hand-picking, but **does not guarantee that each guest will personally take part in farm work**. Any hands-on plantation work must be arranged separately.

## How coffee beans are processed and roasted

After harvesting, the beans are separated from their outer layers, processed and dried. The processing method influences the coffee's eventual taste; moisture, drying time and the quality of the raw materials all matter.

The route passes through a processing area where drying is demonstrated, and a country house with a demonstration of roasting over firewood. Roasting changes the color, aroma and properties of the beans. A demonstration of one traditional method, however, does not mean all batches produced by the farm are roasted only over a wood-fired stove.

Several viewpoints are included along the way, giving visitors a chance to appreciate the coffee-growing landscape as well as the technology.

## Tasting and coffee lemonade

At the end of the visit, travelers sample freshly brewed coffee. You can connect the flavor and aroma with the stages of processing you have just seen. In the main house, the farm also serves **coffee lemonade**, which is included in the excursion.

Comparing aroma, acidity and aftertaste can be rewarding. However, the tour does not specify a fixed number of varieties, cups or brewing methods. It should not be represented as a private professional cupping session with a set number of samples.

## What is included and what needs to be arranged

| Stage | Activities |
|---|---|
| Plantations | Cultivation and picking |
| Production | Processing and drying |
| Roasting | Technique demonstration |
| Finale | Tasting |

**An introduction to coffee production and a tasting** are included. The total duration, price, guiding language and transportation from your hotel must be agreed separately. An afternoon departure does not by itself establish the precise meeting time.

Closed-toe shoes and rain protection are useful for walking among the plants. Confirm the pickup point, trail conditions and whether the tour can proceed during heavy rainfall.

## Why travelers visit this farm in the coffee region

[Salento](/colombia/place/salento/) is located within Colombia's Coffee Cultural Landscape. Farms like this show how agriculture relates to the settlements and livelihoods of local families.

If coffee is the main theme of your journey, compare [coffee tours](/interests/coffee-tours/) and [food and wine trips](/interests/food-and-wine/). Nevertheless, a standalone excursion to El Ocaso provides a complete introduction to coffee production without a need to visit additional plantations.

A walk around Salento or a visit to the Cocora Valley can be arranged as a separate continuation of the day, but **neither is confirmed as part of the El Ocaso product**.

## Frequently asked questions about El Ocaso farm

### What is shown during the visit?

The plantations, hand-picking of coffee cherries, processing, drying, roasting and tasting. Coffee lemonade is served at the end.

### Is a tasting included?

Yes. It is expressly listed in the excursion program.

### At what elevation is the farm?

The published description gives an approximate elevation of **1,500 m** in the Central Andes.

### Is transportation from Salento provided?

A transfer has not been confirmed as included. The meeting point and transportation should be arranged separately.

**[El Ocaso](/colombia/place/el-ocaso-coffee-farm/) can be visited on current Ada Tours journeys of 9, 10 and 11 days.** The farm is in the coffee region near [Salento](/colombia/place/salento/). The visit concludes with a tasting and coffee lemonade.

The main question when choosing a multi-day tour is what you want to see **after** visiting the farm. One itinerary continues to the Rosario Islands, another includes three nights on Barú Island, while the third includes a stay on San Andrés. The time spent in the coffee region and the total number of flights also differ.

## Which tours pass through El Ocaso?

| Tour | What follows the coffee experience |
|---|---|
| [Colombia in 9 days](/colombia/tour/colombia-explorer-9-days/) | Medellín, Rosario Islands |
| [VIP Colombia in 10 days](/colombia/tour/colombia-vip-coffee-cartagena-baru-10-days/) | Cartagena, Barú |
| [Colombia's Many Faces, 11 days](/colombia/tour/colombia-complete-11-days/) | Cartagena, San Andrés, Medellín |

All three itineraries include an excursion to El Ocaso. This is more meaningful than a general mention of the Coffee Triangle: other [Colombia trips](/colombia/tour/) may visit another farm or have no plantation visits at all.

### Nine days: coffee, outdoor activities and an island excursion

The [nine-day program](/colombia/tour/colombia-explorer-9-days/) travels through Bogotá, the coffee region, Medellín and Cartagena. Near Pereira, travelers visit the [Cocora Valley](/colombia/place/cocora-valley/), Salento and El Ocaso. Ziplining and horseback riding across green hills are scheduled as a separate activity.

The Caribbean portion includes a day excursion to the [Rosario Islands](/colombia/place/rosario-islands/), after which guests return to Cartagena. This option suits those who want to combine a farm excursion with active experiences, major cities and a day by the sea. Domestic flights on the itinerary are paid for separately.

### Ten days: the coffee region and three nights on Barú

The [ten-day VIP itinerary](/colombia/tour/colombia-vip-coffee-cartagena-baru-10-days/) combines Bogotá, Pereira, Cartagena and three nights on [Barú Island](/colombia/place/baru-island/). The coffee-region segment includes a journey through Cocora and Salento and a separate excursion to El Ocaso. A hot-air-balloon flight above the coffee plantations is planned for a later stage of the program.

This tour includes private ground transfers and Russian-speaking guided tours in Bogotá and Pereira. Domestic flights Bogotá–Pereira and Pereira–Cartagena, as well as international flights, are not included in the price. These details relate only to this itinerary and cannot automatically be assumed for other VIP products.

### Eleven days: a coffee farm and San Andrés

The [Colombia's Many Faces tour](/colombia/tour/colombia-complete-11-days/) includes El Ocaso on a day visiting Cocora and Salento. The itinerary then features further activities in the coffee region, Cartagena, three nights on [San Andrés](/colombia/place/san-andres/), and Medellín with Guatapé.

This route is suitable for travelers wishing to combine coffee production with a longer stay on an island. There are several transport stages to consider. The number of nights and final price calculation must be agreed before payment; domestic flights are listed as exclusions.

## What makes the farm itself interesting?

El Ocaso is located at approximately **1,500 meters** above sea level in the Central Andes. During the excursion, you learn how coffee cherries are picked by hand, observe processing and drying, and discover the roasting process. A tasting of freshly prepared coffee follows the production demonstration. Coffee lemonade is served at the end.

Exploring the wider coffee region offers other experiences. In the [Cocora Valley](/colombia/place/cocora-valley/), you can see mountain slopes and wax palms, while [Salento](/colombia/place/salento/) offers colorful streets, workshops and viewpoints. These stops may appear alongside the farm in an itinerary, but they are not automatically included in the farm excursion.

El Ocaso is also distinct from the [Pereira coffee farm excursion](/colombia/pereira/pereira-coffee-farm-tour/). The former explores the journey of a coffee cherry to the cup, while the latter places greater emphasis on flavor evaluation and brewing methods. Similar themes do not make these separate excursions interchangeable.

## How to choose a route without unnecessary transfers

For more time in cities and varied activities in the coffee region, compare the **9-day** program. For an island stay following the sightseeing section and the stated VIP package of ground services, explore the **10-day** option. If San Andrés and a longer program appeal to you, compare the **11-day** route.

All itineraries use multiple transportation hubs. Check overnight stays, flight inclusions, guide languages and excursion durations before choosing. Comfortable shoes and rain protection are useful in the damp mountain region; the Caribbean coast requires a different set of belongings.

The [Colombia coffee tours catalog](/interests/coffee-tours/tours/colombia/) contains other coffee-focused options. If visiting El Ocaso specifically is a priority, look for an explicit reference to the farm in the itinerary.

## Frequently asked questions about El Ocaso tours

### Does the excursion include a tasting?

Yes. The [El Ocaso excursion](/colombia/salento/el-ocaso-coffee-farm-tour/) includes an introduction to production and a tasting. Coffee lemonade is served at the end.

### Do all three tours offer the same kind of beach holiday?

No. The nine-day itinerary offers an excursion to the Rosario Islands, the ten-day tour includes three nights on Barú and the eleven-day program includes three nights on San Andrés. These are different kinds of Caribbean experiences.

### Can a coffee-region tour omit El Ocaso?

Yes. A general mention of the coffee region does not guarantee a visit to a specific farm. Check the day-by-day itinerary or select tours from this collection linked to the [El Ocaso excursion](/colombia/salento/el-ocaso-coffee-farm-tour/).

## Excursions in Salento: Cocora Valley and El Ocaso coffee farm

**Salento in Colombia is a convenient place to explore two defining features of the coffee region: wax palms in the cloud forest and coffee production on mountain farms.** We offer two independent excursions in the area. One combines the [Cocora Valley and a walk through Salento](/colombia/pereira/cocora-valley-salento-tour/); the other focuses on [El Ocaso coffee farm](/colombia/salento/el-ocaso-coffee-farm-tour/).

Both experiences reveal the Quindío region, but appeal to different interests. The first is for those who want to see the famous palms, cloud forest and colorful streets. The second explains the coffee cherry's journey from bush to cup. The town itself, its architecture and location are covered separately on the [Salento page](/colombia/place/salento/).

## Excursions available in the catalog

| Excursion | Main theme |
|---|---|
| [Cocora and Salento](/colombia/pereira/cocora-valley-salento-tour/) | Palms, forest, town |
| [El Ocaso farm](/colombia/salento/el-ocaso-coffee-farm-tour/) | Coffee cultivation and production |

["Cocora Valley and Salento: wax palms and cloud forest"](/colombia/pereira/cocora-valley-salento-tour/) is a **five-hour excursion from Pereira** with an English-speaking guide. It includes transportation, a walk along an ecological trail and an introduction to local traditions and crafts. Lunch is paid for separately.

["El Ocaso coffee farm: from cherry to cup"](/colombia/salento/el-ocaso-coffee-farm-tour/) introduces coffee cultivation, processing, drying and roasting. The excursion ends with a tasting and coffee lemonade. A specific departure time and price are not fixed as universal conditions for this excursion, so these details are agreed when selecting a date.

## Cocora Valley: wax palms and cloud forest

The [Cocora Valley](/colombia/place/cocora-valley/) is famous for its tall Quindío wax palms rising above green hills and misty forest. The wax palm is Colombia's national tree and one of the symbols of the Andean coffee region. On clear days the palms stand against mountain scenery; in cloudy weather, mist transforms the trail.

The Cocora excursion includes a meeting with a local eco-guide, a walk along an ecological route and an explanation of wax palm conservation. The program also includes a palm-planting ceremony. Following the nature portion, travelers head to Salento, walk along the colonial streets and explore artisan workshops.

The route begins **in Pereira**, so it should not be confused with an independent visit to the valley from a hotel in Salento. The hotel transfer departs at 9:00. Booking should follow the terms of the [excursion from Pereira](/colombia/pereira/cocora-valley-salento-tour/), rather than assuming pickup is available from any settlement in the coffee region.

## El Ocaso: what happens on a coffee excursion?

At [El Ocaso farm](/colombia/place/el-ocaso-coffee-farm/), visitors explore coffee production while walking among bushes and farm buildings. You learn about cultivation and the hand-picking of cherries, processing, drying and roasting the beans. A tasting follows.

For someone used to seeing coffee only on supermarket shelves, the difference between a fruit and a finished bean is especially interesting. A coffee cherry passes through several processing stages before the drink develops its familiar aroma. A local specialist explains the process, and individual stops demonstrate different stages of production.

The excursion also includes viewpoints, a country house and coffee roasting over firewood. The coffee tasting is included; additional purchases of beans or souvenirs must not be considered included without a specific statement.

## Walking around Salento between excursions

Salento is known for its colorful doors and balconies, workshops and small cafés. After visiting the [Cocora Valley](/colombia/place/cocora-valley/), it is pleasant to return to town, stroll along the old streets and look toward the hills from viewpoints. Such a day combines nature and urban life.

If coffee is your primary interest, prioritize the [El Ocaso excursion](/colombia/salento/el-ocaso-coffee-farm-tour/) and leave some time for Salento itself. If you prefer walking forest trails and seeing wax palms in their natural setting, make the [Cocora Valley](/colombia/pereira/cocora-valley-salento-tour/) the centerpiece.

Colombia's Coffee Cultural Landscape is recognized by UNESCO for its combination of historic farming, mountain geography and regional settlements. However, not every farm or individual street is independently designated as a World Heritage site. The specific itinerary and activities on offer are more important for travelers.

## How to plan your day and what to bring

The coffee region has damp mountain weather, and sunshine may quickly give way to rain and fog. For the Cocora Valley, bring shoes with good traction, lightweight waterproof clothing and water. The coffee farm usually involves fewer lengthy walks, but its paths may also be slippery after rain.

If you plan to take both excursions, check departure times, transportation between stops and the actual duration of the farm visit. **Five hours** is the duration of the "Cocora and Salento" excursion, not the combined time for both products.

Other outings can be found in the [Colombia excursion catalog](/colombia/excursion/) and among [coffee journeys](/interests/coffee-tours/). When comparing [Colombia tours](/colombia/tour/), check whether a specific farm or valley is part of the principal itinerary or offered as a separate visit.

## Frequently asked questions about Salento excursions

### What should I choose: Cocora Valley or a coffee farm?

For natural scenery and wax palms, choose the [Cocora excursion](/colombia/pereira/cocora-valley-salento-tour/). To discover the full coffee production process and enjoy a tasting, choose [El Ocaso](/colombia/salento/el-ocaso-coffee-farm-tour/).

### Which city does the Cocora excursion start from?

The current Ada Tours excursion departs **from Pereira** and includes Salento. Its listing specifies a five-hour route, transportation and an English-speaking guide.

### Is a tasting part of the El Ocaso excursion?

Yes. An introduction to coffee production and a tasting are included in the program. Coffee lemonade is served at the end.

### Can I visit both excursions in one day?

That depends on departure times, the length of the farm visit and transportation connections. They are separate catalog products, so combining them in one day should be arranged separately.

### Does the Cocora Valley require extensive hiking?

The nature excursion involves a walk along an ecological trail, but it is not described as a multi-day trek. Check the exact walking distance and trail conditions for your chosen program.

## Alto de los Ídolos and Mortiño Waterfall: archaeology and nature in Colombia

This Ada Tours excursion combines 2 different experiences in southern Huila Department: a visit to **Alto de los Ídolos Archaeological Park** and **Salto del Mortiño Waterfall**. The route explores the surroundings of [San Agustín](/colombia/place/san-agustin/) and the municipality of Isnos. Ancient stone monuments stand among green hills, cliffs and mountain rivers of the upper Magdalena basin.

The excursion costs **$143 per person**. Discounts may be available for parties of more than one person. The exact duration, transfer arrangements, inclusion of park admission and guide services have not been confirmed for this excursion, so these details must be agreed at booking. Admission charged by the national park as a separate organization cannot automatically be assumed to be part of the Ada Tours price.

## Alto de los Ídolos: the significance of the name

Alto de los Ídolos is in the municipality of Isnos and forms part of the San Agustín region's archaeological complex. Together with San Agustín Archaeological Park itself and the Alto de las Piedras area, it belongs to the cultural heritage of the upper Magdalena River. **This ensemble was designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1995.**

Earthen burial structures, monolithic sarcophagi and carved stone figures survive on the hillside. The Colombian Institute of Anthropology and History (ICANH) identifies **7 burial mounds** and at least **23 stone statues** at Alto de los Ídolos. Their shapes combine human and animal features. These monuments evoke the rituals, beliefs about death and artistic traditions of peoples who lived here before Spanish colonization.

It is important to distinguish **Alto de los Ídolos from the main San Agustín Archaeological Park**: they are related sites within one cultural complex, not the same location. This excursion specifically names Alto de los Ídolos; visits to all the other archaeological zones do not automatically follow from that.

## How to view the stone statues and burial monuments

To discover the archaeological heritage, it is better to examine a few monuments attentively than to try to photograph every statue. Compare facial outlines, poses and carved reliefs; notice the placement of the statues in relation to burial structures and terraces. The precise identities of the figures and meanings of individual symbols remain matters of scholarly interpretation.

This is an open-air museum. Walking is required along paths and grassy areas, which may become wet after rain. ICANH prohibits leaving the designated trails or touching monuments: even stone that looks sturdy is gradually damaged by physical contact. Visitors must not remove objects from the site or interfere with archaeological remains.

For more background, read the [San Agustín guide](/colombia/place/san-agustin/) and explore [culture and history routes](/interests/culture-and-history/). Inclusion of additional museums or parks must be checked against the specific travel offering.

## Mortiño Waterfall: the other side of the journey

**Salto del Mortiño Waterfall** is situated among green mountains near the road connecting San Agustín and Isnos. Its waters descend into a deep gorge surrounded by vegetation. After the archaeological monuments, the experience is entirely different: an open canyon view, moving water and slopes that become particularly vibrant green in wet weather.

The itinerary includes a visit to the waterfall as a separate natural attraction. This **does not confirm swimming under the falls, rappelling or any other extreme activity**. Access to viewpoints depends on road conditions, trails and weather. Near steep drops, remain in designated areas and follow the accompanying guide's instructions.

A water-protected camera or phone is useful for photographs; in fog or after rain, visibility can differ from pictures taken on sunny days. Neither constant water flow nor a completely unobstructed panorama of the gorge can be guaranteed.

## Visiting hours and archaeological park closure dates

According to ICANH, Alto de los Ídolos is open to visitors **from 08:00 to 16:00**, but closes for maintenance on specific dates. In the second half of 2026, the official closure calendar lists **October 21 and 28** and **November 4, 11, 18 and 25**, among other days. The archaeological part of an excursion must therefore be checked against the current calendar even when the nature stop remains accessible.

ICANH publishes its own admission prices, visitor categories and ticketing rules. These relate to the museum and archaeological infrastructure, not the price of the Ada Tours product. Before traveling, establish whether tickets are bought separately, whether a combined ticket applies to several archaeological areas, and which concessions may be available.

## Who will enjoy this excursion?

The route is designed for travelers who want to combine **pre-Columbian history with natural scenery** in a single trip. The two attractions complement each other: stone figures reveal something of ancient societies, while the waterfall offers a view of today's mountain landscape in southern Huila.

Bring closed-toe shoes with non-slip soles, water and light protection against rain and sun. Since duration and transportation details have not been fixed, confirm driving time, walking distances and all expenses before booking.

## Frequently asked questions about Alto de los Ídolos and Mortiño

### Is this the same park as San Agustín?

**No.** Alto de los Ídolos lies near Isnos and is a separate part of the archaeological complex connected with San Agustín. Both belong to the UNESCO-listed heritage.

### How much does the excursion cost?

**$143 per person** is the Ada Tours excursion price. Discounts may be offered to groups of more than one person, with the final terms agreed when booking.

### Is ICANH admission included?

It has not been confirmed that admission is included in the excursion price. Archaeological park admission rates are published separately.

### Can I visit the waterfall when the archaeological park is closed?

The waterfall and archaeological area are different places, but changes to the full excursion or a separate trip to the waterfall must be arranged with the operator. Do not assume the full itinerary can go ahead unchanged on a park closure day.

### What are the walking conditions?

The archaeological site has marked paths; near the waterfall there may be wet ground and viewpoints on uneven terrain. Comfortable shoes are essential, and access to particular sections should be confirmed in advance.

## An excursion in San Agustín: Alto de los Ídolos and Mortiño Waterfall

**San Agustín in Huila Department is known for archaeological monuments from pre-Columbian Colombia.** For an introduction to this heritage, consider the [Alto de los Ídolos and Mortiño Waterfall excursion](/colombia/san-agustin/alto-de-los-idolos-mortino-waterfall-tour/). It combines ancient stone sculptures with a stop among green mountains beside a deep waterfall gorge.

The [San Agustín page](/colombia/place/san-agustin/) describes the town and the historical importance of the region. Here we focus on the specific itinerary: what Alto de los Ídolos is, why it is a separate archaeological heritage location, and how Mortiño Waterfall transforms the experience of the excursion day.

## What sites does the excursion include?

| Stop | What you will see |
|---|---|
| Alto de los Ídolos | Statues and burials |
| Mortiño Waterfall | A cascade in a deep gorge |

**Alto de los Ídolos** lies in the municipality of Isnos, near San Agustín. The archaeological monuments include stone figures, sarcophagi and burial structures. Ancient craftspeople carved human faces, animals and unusual mythological images out of stone; many are associated with funerary traditions.

**Salto del Mortiño** is a waterfall in the mountains of southern Huila. Here, attention shifts from stone carving and the history of human settlement to natural relief: water falls into a green gorge, with slopes enclosing the narrow valley.

Both attractions appear in the title and confirmed description of the same Ada Tours excursion. However, a long trek to the foot of the waterfall and visits to every known archaeological sector in the region are not listed as obligatory parts of the product.

## Alto de los Ídolos and UNESCO heritage

San Agustín Archaeological Park is on the UNESCO World Heritage List. In addition to central San Agustín areas, it includes Alto de los Ídolos and Alto de las Piedras. This matters geographically: monuments left by an ancient culture are spread over several archaeological sites along the upper Magdalena River.

At **Alto de los Ídolos**, large sculptures with human and fantastic features are especially noteworthy. Many figures formed part of burial complexes. Modern understanding of the people who created the monuments is based on archaeological research; assigning each sculpture to an individually named ruler or deity is impossible.

The excursion offers an opportunity to view genuine archaeological remains in their natural setting. Follow the permitted paths and site rules: even stone that appears strong can be damaged by touching ancient reliefs or stepping beyond restricted areas.

## What makes Mortiño Waterfall interesting?

After the archaeological portion, the itinerary changes character. **Mortiño Waterfall** plunges into a gorge between green slopes and is usually viewed from lookout areas at some distance. Humidity, vegetation and the sound of falling water create a strong contrast with the archaeological site.

Do not mistake this excursion for a demanding sporting route to the waterfall. A visit to Mortiño as the second main attraction is included, but descending to the water and tackling a technically difficult trail are not listed as essential parts of the excursion. Such activities can only be discussed if a separate confirmed program is available.

In rainy weather, visibility may change and the ground near viewpoints becomes wet. Shoes with firm grip and a light rain jacket are useful. It is especially important to keep a safe distance from the edge of the gorge.

## How this differs from a general tour of San Agustín

San Agustín is surrounded by archaeological and natural attractions, so the phrase "San Agustín excursion" may refer to different itineraries. A visit to the central archaeological park, Alto de los Ídolos and other locations requires its own schedule. The sites have different approach roads and observation points.

**The Ada Tours itinerary specifically names Alto de los Ídolos and Mortiño.** It suits travelers wishing to combine one remarkable archaeological site with mountain scenery while leaving time for other activities. If you want a full circuit of the UNESCO archaeological monuments, choose a longer itinerary rather than assuming everything is included in this single excursion.

This is a standalone Ada Tours excursion. You can find the exact price and discount information on [its page](/colombia/san-agustin/alto-de-los-idolos-mortino-waterfall-tour/); transfers, meals, guide language and duration are agreed when booking.

## Practical tips before departure

Appreciating the statues takes time and a chance to examine the reliefs without rushing. At elevation in a humid mountain climate, closed-toe shoes, water, sunscreen and rain protection are useful. Before the trip, check access to the archaeological sites and the chosen viewpoint at the waterfall: protected-site rules and road conditions may change.

If San Agustín is one stop on a longer journey through the country, compare [Colombia tours](/colombia/tour/) and the [general excursion catalog](/colombia/excursion/). Check which archaeological site is explicitly named in the itinerary: simply traveling near San Agustín does not guarantee a visit to Alto de los Ídolos.

## Frequently asked questions about the San Agustín excursion

### Is Alto de los Ídolos included in UNESCO World Heritage?

Yes. It is one of the archaeological sites of the San Agustín Archaeological Park World Heritage property, alongside other locations in the region.

### Is the excursion only about archaeological monuments?

No. The [Ada Tours program](/colombia/san-agustin/alto-de-los-idolos-mortino-waterfall-tour/) includes both Alto de los Ídolos and Mortiño Waterfall.

### Is the central San Agustín Archaeological Park included?

Its presence on a general list of regional attractions does not mean it is included in this particular tour. The current excursion specifically focuses on Alto de los Ídolos and Mortiño.

### Do I need to prepare for hiking?

Comfortable shoes are needed to visit archaeological remains and viewpoints; athletic trekking and descending into the gorge are not compulsory. Check the physical demands of the chosen itinerary.

### Can I book the trip with an English-speaking guide?

The guide's language is not explicitly specified for this excursion. It must be agreed before booking; English-language guiding should not be assumed automatically.
